answer: Hypothesis (final, data-grounded): **All 18 of the 18 Experimental Economics studies in the dataset (100%) were conducted in a lab setting** — i.e., none were conducted online. Restricting to the Experimental Economics Replication Project subset (project == 'ee', which coincides exactly with discipline == 'Economics'), every original study has `online.o == 0` (18/18 = 100%), every replication has `online.r == 0` (18/18), all pairs have `same_online == 1` (18/18), and no study used 'online' or 'anyone' subjects in either the original or replication (17 originals used students and 1 used community members — ee.4 "Participation", still a non-online session with `online.o == 0`; all 18 replications used students). Because the schema records no literal "lab" column, "lab setting" is operationalized as "not conducted online," which is the defensible proxy in this data; under that operationalization the proportion of Experimental Economics studies conducted in a lab setting is 1.0 (100%).

payload.workflow: Loaded both CSVs. Scoped to Experimental Economics = project=='ee' (18 studies; set-equal to discipline=='Economics'). Each study = one O/R pair = one row (no lab expansion, no aggregated/drop flags, no duplicates, no missing in relevant fields). Operationalized 'lab setting' as online==0 (no literal lab column exists): verified online.o==0 for 18/18 originals, online.r==0 for 18/18 replications, same_online==1 for 18/18, and subject types free of 'online'/'anyone' (17 students + 1 community original; all student replications). Cross-checked with file 2 (18 'Experimental Economics' rows, no online/subjects fields — corroborates scope only). Computed proportion = 18/18 = 100.0%. Full-file context (dedup by id, n=141): 96.5% non-online overall, ee uniquely 100%.
